A 61-year-old female is hospitalized four hours after her spouse found her following an acetaminophen
overdose in a suicide attempt. She is currently asymptomatic. Her vital signs show blood pressure
103/69 mmHg and heart rate 85/min. Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. Laboratory
results indicate AST and ALT levels of approximately 2500 U/L, APAP level of 160 mcg/mL, and INR of
1.7. The patient is refusing N-acetyl-cysteine (NAC) treatment. What would be the most appropriate
next step in managing this case? Answer Choices: (A) Begin liver transplant evaluation (B) Place
psychiatric hold and proceed with NAC (C) Involve the patient's husband to guide medical care (D)
Document patient refusal and monitor condition (E) Obtain emergency court order for treatment (F)
Transfer to intensive care unit (G) Administer activated charcoal (H) Request ethics committee
consultation (I) Administer NAC (J) Consult psychiatry
 A. Begin liver transplant evaluation
B. Involve the patient's husband to guide medical care
C. Obtain emergency court order for treatment
D. Place psychiatric hold and proceed with NAC
E. Consult psychiatry
F. Administer NAC
G. Document patient refusal and monitor condition
H. Request ethics committee consultation
I. Administer activated charcoal
J. Transfer to intensive care unit
